about: ges, boss, and grasp with missing="em" at ebic_gamma=0.0 against Tetrad 8.0.0's FGES, BOSS, and GRaSP under its EM covariance policy, and against Tetrad's test-wise deletion, test-wise PC, listwise deletion, mean imputation, the complete-data fits of both packages, and the empty graph
build: Andrey pre-release build of 10 November 2026 on the 0.17.0 release branch (version string 0.16.0)

references.ges(missing=\"em\"), boss(missing=\"em\": tetrad-lib 8.0.0, Java 21: FGES, BOSS, GRaSP with SemBicScore under MissingDataPolicy.EM_COVARIANCE at MissingDataSpec.of defaults (ridge 0, tolerance 1e-6, 1,000 iterations, FULL_N), penaltyDiscount 1.0; a one-pass EM estimate of a saturated covariance followed by the search, not structural EM

verdict_rule: per cell and search: D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(reference) per dataset on the datasets both finished; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D over 10,000 resamples lies above 0, better when below, a tie otherwise; fewer than 10 pairs are not judged. A worse row counts only when the same cell on 20 fresh seeds is worse too. Floor: the interval of SHD(Andrey) - SHD(empty graph) must lie below 0; it decides a judged row at 15 variables and 100 rows where the reference's own interval lies below 0, and is reported elsewhere. A search passes when no judged row is worse again and no judged row fails the floor.

ges(missing=\"em\").limit: at the plain BIC on Erdos-Renyi graphs of mean degree 4 the result is rarely better than the empty graph (5 of 54 cells); on the complete data the plain search's mean SHD is at or above the empty graph's in 4 of those 9 settings; at mean degree 2 it is below the empty graph in 51 of 54 cells

fresh_seeds.about: no row is worse than the reference, so none ran again; the worse rows against test-wise PC, a baseline, were not rerun

refits.about: three fits failed on a read of the Python environment's files and were fit again; their records replace the failed ones
